title: Disinformation and fake news
subtitle: Lying in the viral age
subject: comprendreLeMonde
description: False information spreads 6 times faster than the truth on social media. Why, and how to protect yourself?

hero.hook: An MIT study showed that fake news travels 6 times faster than the truth on Twitter. Here's why.

blocks.text: Lying to serve a political purpose is nothing new: traces of it have been found since Antiquity. But the Internet and social networks have changed the situation: false information no longer only circulates from a State to its population, it now spreads horizontally, between citizens.

This shift has created a world where the truth sometimes seems optional in the face of virality. Understanding how **misinformation** spreads, and who benefits from it, has become essential to preserving trust between citizens.

sections.title: Why lies travel faster than the truth

blocks.text: We must distinguish disinformation, deliberately disseminated to manipulate, from simple honest errors. The success of this fake news relies on what researchers call the attention economy: social media algorithms are designed to maximize screen time, and our brains respond more strongly to emotion and shock than to nuance.
A study by  published in 2018 showed that fake news spreads about 6 times faster than verified news on Twitter because it appears fresher and more emotionally intense. [[MIT]]

Algorithms also lock Internet users into : they only show them content confirming their already existing opinions. A person convinced of a conspiracy theory then sees each new false information as additional proof, which makes any subsequent correction very difficult. [[Filter bubbles]]

sections.title: An industry of lies, between States and profit

blocks.text: Disinformation has become a real industry. States like Russia, through the Internet Research Agency, have created thousands of fake automated accounts to stir up tensions within Western democracies, without even trying to defend a specific camp: the goal is often to create chaos and make people believe that “everyone is lying”.

blocks.caption: False information spreads in seconds on social networks.

blocks.text: There is also a purely lucrative dimension: in the town of Veles, in North Macedonia, young entrepreneurs created sensationalist sites in 2016 without any political conviction, solely to earn money through traffic generated on social networks. The lie then becomes a simple profitable commodity.

sections.title: How to separate fact from fiction

blocks.text: Faced with this deluge, the world of information is organizing itself. **fact-checking**, that is to say the verification of facts, has become a journalistic discipline in its own right. Agencies like  or specialized editorial offices use image search tools to detect fakery and analyze suspicious content. [[AFP]]

But the race between attack and defense remains unequal. The appearance of , videos rigged by artificial intelligence where a person is made to say anything with disturbing realism, makes the distinction between true and false more and more difficult for an untrained eye. [[Deepfakes]]

sections.title: Finding confidence in a world of images

blocks.text: The long-term effect of misinformation is profound: we are now talking about a **post-truth** era, where objective facts sometimes carry less weight than emotions and personal beliefs. This generalized relativization weakens the confidence necessary to tackle global challenges like the climate or public health together.

The most solid answer remains media education: learning to verify a source, cross-referencing several pieces of information, and understanding how algorithms work. Some also rely on content certification technologies, to guarantee the origin of a video from its creation. In the meantime, everyone's vigilance remains the first line of defense.

False information spreads on average 6 times faster than the truth on social networks, because it exploits our emotions and our thirst for novelty. Faced with deepfakes and troll farms, media education remains the best weapon to preserve collective trust.
